entries.en: Hiwada, who had slipped into the building in front of the station, had no choice but to rush into the restroom. Left alone, Takano found herself knocking on the conference room door, forced to stand calmly for introductions. The representatives from the client company directed a mix of expectation and caution towards her. It was an unprecedented situation for the company, having her lead the explanation at a client meeting. They say that even dust can accumulate into a mountain, and the weight of Hiwada's daily small anxieties now bore down on him like the weight of a room. An uneasy silence, entirely uncharacteristic of the sales department that valued moderation, hung in the air. Only the second hand of the clock ticked away diligently behind Takano.

entries.en: Takano gently brushed her fingertips over the documents laid out on the table, as if they were papers she was seeing for the first time. In reality, she had never read their contents even once. The other person adjusted the cuffs of their suit lightly, patiently waiting for her next words. She was thrown a question that she couldn't possibly answer, and all that stood out in Takano's vision was the oddly vivid pattern of the wallpaper in the conference room. Nevertheless, she raised the corners of her mouth and maintained her composure as a sales employee. That lady-like smile barely held the situation together, teetering on the edge of a cliff.

entries.en: In the restroom's stall, Hiwada was curled up on the toilet seat, hugging his knees. The sound of his own pitiful groans echoing through the wall only made him shrink further. The memory of being rejected by fifty companies during his job search was now etched in his body like a gene, causing his stomach to react to even the slightest adversity. Did it even matter if he tried hard? — Such thoughts began to swirl in his mind, pulsing in rhythm with the pain in his gut. From down the hallway, he faintly heard Takano's voice searching for him. Even so, he couldn't muster the resolve to open the door.

entries.en: Hiwada's smartphone, locked away in the private room, vibrated once in his inner pocket. When he took it out, a short message in hiragana from Takano appeared on the screen. There were no words of reproach or urgency; only the simple fact that she was "waiting." The phrase "Let's do our best together," which she had exchanged with him in the job-hunting waiting room, suddenly surfaced from the depths of distant memory. At the very least, Takano had been coming to the company every day without quitting, even while aware that it wasn't the right fit for her. In contrast, here he was, merely whispering that he wanted to quit without planning anything at all.

entries.en: As she watched, Takano collided head-on with a salaryman walking from the front. The man's café latte flew through the air, and large stains spread across both Takano's white blouse and the man's suit. All eyes in the vicinity turned to them, and Hiwada couldn't help but gasp. Takano hurriedly bowed her head, repeatedly apologizing. The man who had been bumped into clearly looked displeased, but he wasn't so flustered as to lose his composure and shout. Hiwada could only watch from a short distance, torn between rushing over or pretending not to see.

entries.en: When he arrived at the office, Hatoyama had Takano sit in a chair and began explaining the stain removal process with the meticulousness of a home economics teacher. He demonstrated each step, from the components of café latte to the properties of the fabric. Hiwada watched this unexpected domestic skill of his senior from the corner of his desk, feeling impressed. Colleagues passing by also stopped to watch, curious about what was happening. Hatoyama's fingers moved with unwavering precision, and the way the handkerchief absorbed the oil from the fabric was reminiscent of a craftsman's technique. Yet, without even a hint of breathlessness, Hatoyama shifted his focus to Takano's collar. Mornings in the sales department often begin with scenes like this.

entries.en: Hatoyama's work continued as he lightly pressed a wet tissue to transfer the dirt. Despite the training supervisor sweating on his forehead, Takano rested his hands on the armrest and stared intently with a serious expression. He showed no sign of wanting to help, nor did he shrink back in apology. This unflinching demeanor had become increasingly mysterious to Hiwada as the days went by. Was it natural, or was it a calculated boldness? Hiwada still couldn't make a judgment. Finally, Hatoyama pinched his collar and lightly adjusted it, nodding in satisfaction. The stains had completely vanished without a trace.

Unable to resist his curiosity, Hiwada also left his seat and strained to listen from a distance. Among the colleagues in the sales department, whispers about who Takano was began to circulate at various desks. Eventually, Hatoyama seemed to sense something and carefully chose his words to ask if he could see the locker. Takano responded without hesitation, and the two headed straight to the locker room. The mornings in the office always began with such small mysteries surrounding her.

Inside, several suits identical to the one Takano was currently wearing were hanging at equal intervals. The sight of the same clothes lined up gave off an almost ritualistic intensity. As the start of work approached, colleagues began to show their faces one after another. Hiwada decided to save the continuation of this observation diary for the afternoon and returned to his seat.

entries.en: Shortly after starting the search, Takano's hands came to a stop. She stared intently at the screen, wearing a serious expression, and slowly stood up with that same look on her face. Without hesitation, she walked towards Hatoyama. The surrounding colleagues sensed that something was about to happen again and discreetly eased their work. Hiwada, too, had unknowingly stopped typing on the keyboard. Everyone had already learned that every word from Takano was a small event for this department. The atmosphere in the sales department suddenly became tense.

entries.en: Hatoyama blinked and tried to imagine the words he was about to hear in his mind. Given Takano's tone, there must be a significant incident waiting to be revealed. The surrounding colleagues also looked up from their screens, listening intently. Hiwada realized once again that this person fundamentally lacked the IT vocabulary in Japanese. While the company's sluggish sales might not be solely due to this department, at the very least, Takano's work efficiency had always been at rock bottom. Even so, Hatoyama never raised his voice and patiently showed his willingness to wait for the other person's words.

entries.en: A few days later, an incident occurred in which Ukaï suddenly designated Takano as his companion for a sales meeting. It was impossible for anyone to understand why Ukaï, known for his solitary approach within the company, would choose none other than Takano. Takano himself sat behind Ukaï with his usual calm demeanor. The two were guided to a conference room, facing the materials spread out on the table. As for Hiwada, he was scheduled to attend a different business negotiation with Kijitani, but he couldn't help but keep an eye on the two from a distance. Kijitani came over to Hiwada's seat to check the materials. With no idea of what was about to happen, Hiwada quietly closed his documents.

entries.en: Hiwada called up the client information on his laptop and turned the screen towards Kijitani. FREEDOM MODE Inc. is an unusual presence in the IT industry, and the president has been known as a rebel in the field since his youth. Recently, he has prohibited sales employees from wearing suits or jackets, insisting that everyone in the company dress casually in their own clothes. Even Suzaku, having caught wind of the conversation, peeked out from across the floor, stretching his neck with keen interest. Hiwada was desperately trying to decipher Uka's intention to bring Takano to a company with such a corporate culture all by himself. Within the sales department, the combination of these two seemed like an exceedingly dangerous pairing.

entries.jp: やがて鵜飼は自らのブレザーを羽織り直し、髪を整え、まるで戦場に赴くかのような険しい表情で立ち上がった。その姿を目の当たりにした鷹野は、ぽかんと口を開けたまま、しばらく声を出せずにいる。営業部の同僚たちも、いつもとは違う鵜飼の気迫にざわりと空気を変えた。鵜飼は一切構わず、机の上の資料を確認して席を離れる。鶸田は、この二人の初めての同行がどんな戦になるのか、予感すら立てられないでいた。鵜飼と鷹野は、この会社では珍しい一対の組み合わせだった。鳩山は何かを言いかけ、いったん口をつぐんだ。

entries.en: Eventually, Ukaï adjusted his blazer, tidied his hair, and stood up with a fierce expression as if heading into battle. Upon witnessing this, Takano stood there with his mouth agape, unable to speak for a while. The colleagues in the sales department also felt the atmosphere shift with Ukaï's unusual intensity. Ignoring everyone, Ukaï checked the documents on the desk and left his seat. Hiwada couldn't even begin to predict what kind of battle this first outing for the two would turn into. Ukaï and Takano were a rare pairing in this company. Hatoyama started to say something but fell silent for a moment.

entries.chapter_title: 5. カフェラテと鳩山先輩
entries.jp: 鵙尾は、鵜飼の頼みが降ってきた瞬間から、あからさまに機嫌を悪くしていた。カジュアルな服装で会社に来ているのは自分だけだと突きつけられたのも面白くない。しかし鷹野本人が困っている様子を見せると、鵙尾の表情はふっと緩んだ。二人の間には、鶸田にはまだ読み解けない微妙な空気が流れていた。鵜飼の頭を下げる姿は、営業部でも滅多に見られない光景である。誰もが手を止め、事の成り行きに耳をそばだてていた。鷹野はやがて、鵙尾の傍らへとおずおずと歩み寄っていく。

entries.en: Mogio had clearly been in a bad mood since the moment Ukai's request had come down. It was also frustrating to be reminded that he was the only one in casual clothes at the office. However, when he saw Takano looking troubled, Mogio's expression softened slightly. A subtle tension flowed between the two that Hiwada still couldn't decipher. It was a rare sight to see Ukai bowing his head, even in the sales department. Everyone stopped what they were doing and leaned in to listen to the unfolding situation. Eventually, Takano timidly approached Mogio's side.

It was quite absurd that he was the only one in a suit at a client meeting. From the corner of the office, he could faintly hear Mogio pleading with his colleagues for clothes. Hatoyama had switched to the side of those seeing them off, wearing a smile as if he were sending his daughter off on a school trip.

entries.en: Only Ukai, Hatoyama, and Hiwada remained on the floor. Hiwada suddenly looked down at himself and realized he was still in his suit. Being the only one dressed as a proper businessman while visiting an IT company would clearly make him stand out as a salesperson. For a few seconds, as he hesitated to speak up, countless futures spun around in Hiwada's mind.

entries.en: Ukai led Hiwada through the floors of other departments, visiting colleagues who seemed flexible with their casual attire one after another. The senior they were aiming for pulled out several options from the back of the locker and lined them up in front of Hiwada with a sense of amusement. Hiwada was honestly starting to feel dizzy from the flashy hoodies and T-shirts that kept appearing. Ukai remained expressionless, simply keeping an eye on the time. On the other side of the fitting room curtain, there was a sense that Takano was slowly adjusting their outfit. The women from the sales department began to gather at the entrance of the locker room, half curious. Hiwada finished changing and repeatedly checked for any discomfort in the unfamiliar reflection in the mirror.

entries.chapter_title: 5. カフェラテと鳩山先輩
entries.jp: 鵜飼は苦い顔をしつつ、それでも礼を口にした。鵙尾は満足そうに腕を組み、二人の後ろ姿を見送る。鶸田は、鵜飼のあのプライドの高さが古風な言葉に化けたことに、内心少なからず驚いていた。二人がもと仲の良い関係だったことは、以前から先輩たちの噂で聞かされている。それがどうしていまのような険悪さに至ったのか、今日の一件を見ても答えは見つからない。鶸田はこのバトルにこれ以上巻き込まれるのはうんざりだと思いつつも、頭のどこかで謎解きを始めてしまっていた。営業部の人間関係というのは、思っていたよりずっと複雑な織物のようだった。

entries.en: Ukai made a bitter face, yet still expressed his gratitude. Mokuo crossed his arms with a satisfied look, watching the two of them leave. Hiwada was inwardly surprised that Ukai's high pride had transformed into such old-fashioned words. He had heard from his seniors about how the two used to have a good relationship, but he couldn't find an answer as to how it had come to such a hostile state, even after witnessing today's incident. While Hiwada felt fed up with being further drawn into this battle, a part of his mind had already begun to unravel the mystery. The relationships within the sales department seemed to be a much more complex tapestry than he had anticipated.

entries.en: Ukai quickly started walking, and Takano and Hiwada hurriedly chased after him. Hatoyama watched the three of them head toward the elevator hall from in front of the door. Hiwada's question about why the two of them, who were同期, had created such distance between themselves continued to grow. The sound of their footsteps stepping out into the city center echoed in different tempos.

entries.jp: タクシーを降りた三人の前に、独特なデザインの本社ビルが現れた。エントランスをくぐると、社内の壁には巨大な「呪」の一字が掲げられ、鶸田は思わず立ち止まる。行き交う社員たちの服装は、一人ひとりがまるで音楽フェスの帰りのように自由で、鶸田のスーツだけが完全に浮いている。鷹野は借り物の格好にも動じることなく、周囲を興味深そうに見回している。鵜飼は無表情で先を進み、案内係の女性に会釈をした。会議室に案内されるまでの短い廊下で、鶸田は自分の心拍数が上がっているのを感じていた。自由な社風というのが、これほどまでに人を落ち着かなくさせるとは思ってもみなかった。

entries.en: In front of the three who got out of the taxi, a uniquely designed headquarters building appeared. As they passed through the entrance, a giant character for "curse" was displayed on the wall inside, causing Hiwada to involuntarily stop. The attire of the employees coming and going was so free that each person looked as if they had just returned from a music festival, and Hiwada's suit stood out completely. Takano, undeterred by his borrowed outfit, looked around with interest. Ukai moved ahead with a blank expression and nodded to a female guide. As they walked down the short corridor leading to the conference room, Hiwada felt his heart rate increasing. He never imagined that such a free-spirited company culture could make someone feel so unsettled.

entries.en: Hatoiyama was the first to greet the three who returned to the office. After hearing about the events with the client, Hatoiyama let out a sigh of relief. His concern was less about whether they had achieved results in sales and more about the fact that Takano had returned safely, which was very much in line with Hatoiyama's character. Hiwada returned to his desk and finally relaxed his shoulders, which had been tense under his shirt. Hiwada thought that the negotiations at that free-spirited company would be talked about for years to come. Even five or ten years from now, he felt that the exchanges of "freedom" would be hard to forget. Another day in the sales department passed, becoming even more intense.

entries.en: Hiwada pondered over Hatoyama's words for a while. It seemed that finding a place where Takano could be of help had become almost like a parental instinct for him. Rather than making him a competent salesperson, it felt closer to wanting to ensure he could work happily. Hiwada suddenly realized again that there were such seniors in this company. However, the atmosphere in the sales department was not so simply warming up. From across the floor, Ukai's footsteps were coming straight toward them. Everyone was keenly aware of the shift in the air.

entries.en: Ukai pinpointed the location of the test and quickly approached Mogeoi. The displeasure she had been holding back suddenly erupted as she arrived. Mogeoi, on the other hand, sat calmly in his chair as if he had anticipated this. Hiwada held his breath at his desk, secretly watching the unfolding situation. The other colleagues in the sales department also strained to listen while pretending to be busy with their paperwork. Although this argument between the two was a regular occurrence in the sales department, it seemed to grow more intense each time, as if they had never heard the word "boredom." Despite being同期, Ukai and Mogeoi were the most mismatched pair in the company.

entries.en: After Hato-yama saw Mokuo off with a troubled smile, this scene had become as regular an occurrence for the sales department as the morning assembly. Between Ukai and Mokuo lay a past that others could not intrude upon. Despite being colleagues, the distance between them had persisted for years, leaving only the options to either speak or ignore each other. Hiwada suddenly imagined what the two of them were like in their youth, but it didn't quite come together in his mind. The past, known only through the gossip of the sales department, always appeared somewhat hazy. Even so, the atmosphere between the two now certainly seemed to carry some kind of pain.

entries.en: The story of Suzaku dates back to when the two had just joined the company. At that time, Ukai and Maki were on such friendly terms that they called each other by their first names. They were so close that they were often the subject of gossip within the company, almost like a pair of sisters. One day at a drinking party, Suzaku was teasing Ukai—no, Akane—about her romantic failures. Maki was still called Yumi and was also present at that gathering. Akane's love stories were always a source of laughter, and that night, carefree voices filled a corner of the izakaya.

As for Takano, he seemed to have some urgent plans, grabbing his bag and leaving with a light step. The phrase "for the koi" caused the air in the office to freeze for a few seconds. entries.jp: 鷹野が去ったあとの営業部は、いつものざわつきを取り戻していた。話題は自然と、彼女の恋の相手のことへと流れていく。誰も詳しくは知らないが、それぞれ勝手な推測を口にしていくうちに、話はいつしか鷹野のプライベート全般に広がった。募金活動をしていた、炊き出しを手伝っていた、といった目撃談まで飛び出す始末である。鵜飼はそれを聞くにつれ、じわじわと表情を険しくしていった。働かない同僚の給料が、自分たちの汗から出ていると気づいたときの理不尽さは、うんざりの一言では収まらない。鶸田は、この話題がどこへ着地するのか、内心でハラハラし始めていた。

entries.en: After Takano left, the sales department regained its usual buzz. The conversation naturally shifted to her romantic interest. Although no one knew the details, as each person voiced their own wild speculations, the discussion eventually expanded to encompass all aspects of Takano's private life. Stories even emerged about her participating in fundraising activities and helping with food distribution. As Ukai listened, his expression gradually grew more severe. The absurdity of realizing that the salary of a non-working colleague was coming from their own hard work was beyond frustrating. Hiwada began to feel anxious about where this topic would ultimately lead.

entries.en: Even after the morning assembly-like presentation was over, a slight embarrassment lingered in the air of the sales department. No one could come to a clear understanding of how the system of quantifying gratitude would change their daily language, and that topic was not brought up again that day. Hiwada returned his gaze to the project materials, struggling with the unfamiliar diagrams. As he immersed himself in the task of rewriting and erasing a line in the proposal, only the hands of the clock moved steadily forward. Several days passed in this manner.

entries.jp: サンキューポイント、通称サンポ——導入から幾日も経たぬうちに、営業部の会話は「ありがとう」で細やかに彩られるようになった。しかし、鵜飼の目には、その光景があくまで作り物のように映っていた。誰かの労を素直に労うという行為が、数字と景品の間で薄まっていく——その予感を胸に、彼はキーボードから手を離さぬまま画面を睨んでいた。廊下からは、また新しい足音が近づいてくる。

entries.en: The Thank You Points, commonly known as Sanpo—within just a few days of their introduction, the conversations in the sales department became delicately adorned with "thank yous." However, to Uka, that scene appeared nothing more than a facade. The act of genuinely appreciating someone's efforts was becoming diluted between numbers and prizes—holding that premonition in his heart, he continued to stare at the screen without taking his hands off the keyboard. From the hallway, new footsteps were approaching once again.

entries.en: Since the exchange of Sanpo began, small loans and borrowings within the department have increased. Every time they exchanged words of appreciation, the gazes calculating the next number to come back intertwined more than the gratitude itself. While it wasn't a matter grand enough to be called ethics, Hiwada could certainly feel the weight of the "thank you" spoken from the neighboring seat becoming lighter. He set the documents face down and looked up at the ceiling.

entries.en: Hiwada adjusted his briefcase with a wry smile at Hatoyama's voice, which was a mix of disbelief and admiration. It had become a part of his daily routine to head out for business negotiations with Takano. Even though he had only been with the company for six months, just the fact of going out with a junior made him feel a sense of pride. The client was on the third floor of a building, conveniently close to the station. He had gone over the arrangements in his mind countless times. If he could get through today without any issues, it would be another achievement added to his record at the company—this was what Hiwada genuinely believed.

Takano quietly followed half a step behind Hiwada, as usual. As for Suzak, he was next to him, clutching a bag of snacks and devouring it with the determination to finish the large bag all by himself. A few printed job listings were stacked in the corner of the documents.

entries.jp: 鷹野の呑気な発言に、鶸田は返す言葉を失った。目の前の女は、この状況の重さを一片も理解していないらしい。開発部に転向するか、転職するか、道はそのどちらかしかない――部長の言葉を頭の中で幾度も繰り返すうち、鶸田は自分の思考が空回りしていくのを感じた。四十社、五十社と面接に頭を下げ続けたあの日々を、もう一度なぞる自分の姿を想像しただけで、体の芯からうんざりした。転職市場をまた一からやり直すだけの気力など、正直、どこにも残っていない。今の会社にしがみつくしか道はない、というのが正直な結論だった。

entries.en: Hiwada was at a loss for words in response to Takano's carefree remark. It seemed that the woman in front of him had no understanding of the gravity of the situation. The only paths available were to either switch to the development department or change jobs—repeating the department head's words in his mind, Hiwada felt his thoughts spinning in circles. Just imagining himself retracing the days of bowing his head at interviews with forty or fifty companies made him feel utterly exhausted to the core. Honestly, he had no energy left to start over in the job market from scratch. The only honest conclusion he could come to was that he had no choice but to cling to his current company.
